extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, implementers, licensing negotiators, in-house and external counsel, and policymakers working with SEPs and FRAND licensing
extracted.subtask_description: Practical overview of Standard Essential Patents (SEPs) and FRAND licensing: definitions, methodologies for determining FRAND royalties, drafting considerations for patents likely to become SEPs, best practices for licensing negotiations, SDO disclosure rules, litigation strategies, and recent policy trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Standard Essential Patent (SEP)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Standard Essential Patent (SEP) is a patent that protects an invention essential to the implementation of a particular technology standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEPs cover technologies in standards; essentiality means an implementer must practice the claimed invention to comply with the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAND obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: SEP owners must license their technologies under conditions that are fair, reasonable, and non-discriminatory (FRAND).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FRAND framework seeks to balance SEP owners' rights to recoup R&D investments with implementers' access to standardized technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of addressing hold-up and hold-out
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and mitigate two central problems: hold-up (SEP owner extracting supra-FRAND royalties via threat of injunction) and hold-out (implementer refusing to negotiate in good faith).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRAND policies and case law aim to prevent hold-up (e.g., limits on injunctive relief; antitrust scrutiny) and to address hold-out (possible injunctions where implementer is unwilling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-Down approach for FRAND royalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocates a per-unit royalty based on the SEP owner's proportionate share of all essential patents; divides a cumulative reasonable royalty by patent count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often produces lower royalties; suitable where one wants to cap cumulative royalty burden across all patents implementing the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparable license approach for FRAND royalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses arm's-length licenses for comparable portfolios to set royalty rates, excluding licenses suspected of being affected by hold-up pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often produces higher royalties than top-down; requires careful selection/exclusion of tainted licenses and comparable portfolio adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate claim chart mapping (SEP drafting)
rubrics_metrics.description: When drafting patents likely to become SEPs, anticipate that claims will be mapped to the standard via claim charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft claims and specification so that mapping to standard-essential elements is clear and defensible in licensing and litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard's terminology in patent drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ terminology from the relevant standard in the specification and claims where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using standard terminology facilitates claim-charting and reduces disputes over what constitutes essential subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover both upstream and downstream implementations
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft claims to encompass both upstream (e.g., chipset) and downstream (e.g., device) implementations of the standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad coverage helps capture real-world implementations and supports portfolio licensing strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture mandatory features of the standard (avoid optional features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus claims on mandatory features of the standard and avoid drafting only for optional features which are less likely to be essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory-feature coverage increases the likelihood of essentiality determinations; optional-feature claims are weaker candidates for SEP status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide claim charts showing essentiality (licensing best practice for SEP owners)
rubrics_metrics.description: SEP owners should provide claim charts demonstrating how claims map to the standard and why they are essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim charts are a primary way to establish essentiality and support licensing demands and litigation positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer FRAND terms early (licensing best practice for SEP owners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make FRAND licensing offers at an early stage in negotiations with implementers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early offers can reduce perceived hold-up risk and support a good-faith negotiation record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document negotiation in good faith (licensing best practice for SEP owners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep written records of negotiation steps and offers to demonstrate good-faith licensing efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation is important in FRAND disputes and can be decisive under frameworks like Huawei v. ZTE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider portfolio licensing (licensing best practice for SEP owners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer licensing on a portfolio basis rather than by single patents where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portfolio licensing can simplify negotiations, provide discounts, and address cumulative royalty concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use established arbitration processes (licensing best practice for SEP owners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on arbitration or established dispute-resolution processes to determine FRAND terms when negotiations stall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increased use of arbitration is a recent trend; arbitration can provide finality and neutral determination of FRAND.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in good faith negotiations (licensing best practice for implementers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementers should negotiate constructively and document offers and counter-offers showing good-faith engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing willingness to negotiate can prevent courts from granting injunctive relief against implementers (per Huawei v. ZTE guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-offer with FRAND terms (licensing best practice for implementers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to SEP owners' proposals with specific FRAND counter-offers rather than refusing to engage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete FRAND counter-offers help frame negotiations and reduce hold-out allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document the negotiation process (licensing best practice for implementers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records of communications, offers, and rationale during licensing discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation supports an implementer’s defense against injunctions and FRAND-related claims of bad faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider portfolio license discounts (licensing best practice for implementers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek discounts or favorable terms when negotiating portfolio licenses rather than single-patent deals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portfolio discounts address cumulative royalty burdens and can yield mutually acceptable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Standard Development Organizations (SDOs) (licensing best practice for implementers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage SDO resources, disclosures, and commitments when assessing essentiality and FRAND obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SDOs often maintain records of disclosures and commitments that are relevant evidence in FRAND disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDO disclosure and commitment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of Standards Development Organizations (e.g., ETSI, IEEE, ITU) must disclose essential patents and commit to license on FRAND terms; failure to disclose may render patents unenforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with SDO policies is critical; non-disclosure can have serious enforceability consequences in litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold-up: court and antitrust responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold-up occurs when an SEP owner threatens injunctions to extract supra-FRAND royalties; courts may limit injunctive relief and antitrust authorities may scrutinize such conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEP owners should be mindful that aggressive injunction strategies risk antitrust exposure and judicial limitations on relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold-out: implementer unwillingness and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold-out occurs when an implementer refuses to negotiate in good faith; courts may allow injunctions in cases of unwilling licensees and have set negotiation-process requirements (e.g., Huawei v. ZTE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers must follow prescribed negotiation steps to avoid being treated as unwilling licensees under EU case law and other precedents.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEP litigation strategy for patent owners: establish essentiality with claim charts
rubrics_metrics.description: In litigation, patent owners should establish essentiality through clear claim-chart evidence mapping claims to the standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong essentiality evidence supports damages claims and defenses against challenges to enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEP litigation strategy for patent owners: file counter-claims against unwilling licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners may file counter-claims (e.g., for breach of contract or infringement) against implementers that refuse to license on FRAND terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counter-claims can be part of a broader enforcement strategy, but must be balanced against antitrust and forum-selection considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEP litigation strategy for patent owners: seek licensing in established jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring licensing claims in jurisdictions known for established SEP jurisprudence (e.g., UK, China).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of forum can materially affect remedies and FRAND determinations; forum-shopping risks include anti-suit and anti-anti-suit injunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEP litigation strategy for patent owners: use international arbitration
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider international arbitration as a venue for resolving FRAND disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arbitration is increasingly used for FRAND determination and can provide neutral, enforceable awards across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEP litigation strategy for implementers: challenge essentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementers should challenge whether asserted patents are actually essential to the standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidating essentiality or narrowing claim scope can reduce licensing exposure and damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEP litigation strategy for implementers: seek anti-suit injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use anti-suit injunctions as a defensive tool to prevent parallel proceedings in other jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-suit and anti-anti-suit injunctions are part of the modern SEP litigation playbook but raise complex comity and enforceability issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEP litigation strategy for implementers: use IPR/PGR to challenge validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue inter partes review (IPR) or post-grant review (PGR) to attack validity of asserted SEPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative validity challenges can be faster, cost-effective ways to limit or eliminate asserted patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of major SEP precedents
rubrics_metrics.description: Be familiar with landmark cases (e.g., Microsoft v. Motorola, Apple v. Samsung, Huawei v. ZTE, Unwired Planet v. Huawei) that shape FRAND/SEP law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precedents inform methodologies for royalty determination, injunctive relief limitations, and negotiation-process requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor recent developments and policy trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Track trends such as increased use of arbitration for FRAND, China's growing role as a FRAND adjudicator, anti-anti-suit injunctions, the USPTO/DOJ/NIST joint policy statements, and proposed EU SEP regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stay current because evolving policy and jurisdictional practices materially affect SEP enforcement and licensing strategy.
